children: A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after artificial intelligence and semiconductor stocks pulled back from the previous session's sharp rally, dragging down technology-heavy indexes. CNBC reported that the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.5% and the S&P 500 declined 1.2%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average traded around the flatline. Nvidia shares dropped more than 7% after surging 31% in the previous session following Jensen Huang's return as CEO, while Anthropic shares fell 9%, breaking below its IPO price.

Tom Hulick, CEO of Strategy Asset Managers, told CNBC that Nvidia still has "a lot of things to worry about" regarding corporate governance. Mark Haefele, chief investment officer at UBS Global Wealth Management, said in a note that he expects greater differentiation between established platforms and companies dependent on debt, scarce capacity or continued speculative growth.

A pullback in artificial intelligence and semiconductor stocks can weigh on industrial companies that supply manufacturing equipment, electronic components or power systems for data centers. Share prices across a sector often decline together when investors reduce exposure to capital spending themes and turn more selective on growth.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.

Gas and liquid handling company Ichor Holdings fell 16.3%.

Ichor Holdings’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 87 moves greater than 5% over the last year. But moves this big are rare even for Ichor Holdings and indicate this news significantly impacted the market’s perception of the business.

Ichor Holdings is up 29.1% since the beginning of the year, but at $26.36 per share, it is still trading 76.5% below its 52-week high of $112.28 from June 2026. Despite the year-to-date gain, investors who bought $1,000 worth of Ichor Holdings’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at only $530.71.
